verses.text: Then Jacob called for his sons and said, "Gather around so that I can tell you what will happen to you in the days to come:
Come together and listen, O sons of Jacob; listen to your father Israel.
Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.
Uncontrolled as the waters, you will no longer excel, because you went up to your father's bed, onto my couch, and defiled it.
Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.
May I never enter their council; may I never join their assembly. For they kill men in their anger, and hamstring oxen on a whim.
Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will disperse them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Judah, your brothers shall praise you. Your hand shall be on the necks of your enemies; your father's sons shall bow down to you.
Judah is a young lion— my son, you return from the prey. Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?
The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch. He washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships; his border shall extend to Sidon.
Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.
He saw that his resting place was good and that his land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the burden and submitted to labor as a servant.
Dan shall provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
He will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse's heels so that its rider tumbles backward.
I await Your salvation, O LORD.
Gad will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels.
Asher's food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies.
Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.
Joseph is a fruitful vine— a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
The archers attacked him with bitterness; they aimed at him in hostility.
Yet he steadied his bow, and his strong arms were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, in the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,
by the God of your father who helps you, and by the Almighty who blesses you, with blessings of the heavens above, with blessings of the depths below, with blessings of the breasts and womb.

The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince of his brothers.
Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder."
These are the tribes of Israel, twelve in all, and this was what their father said to them. He blessed them, and he blessed each one with a suitable blessing.
Then Jacob instructed them, "I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite.
The cave is in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. This is the field Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah are buried, and there I buried Leah.
The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the Hittites."
When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Joseph and his brothers (Genesis 37 to 50)
context.audience: Israel, the twelve tribes, learning how their fathers came down to Egypt and how God turned evil to good
context.setting: Jacob calls his sons together: “Gather around so that I can tell you what will happen to you in the days to come” (v.1). In poetry he speaks a word over each of the twelve. Reuben, the firstborn, loses his place because “you went up to your father’s bed” (vv.3-4). Simeon and Levi are cursed for their violent anger and will be scattered (vv.5-7). “Judah, your brothers shall praise you,” a young lion, and “The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his” (vv.8-12). Zebulun by the sea, Issachar the strong donkey, Dan who judges, Gad, Asher and Naphtali each receive a short word (vv.13-21), with a sudden prayer in the middle: “I await Your salvation, O LORD” (v.18). “Joseph is a fruitful vine,” attacked by archers but made strong by “the Mighty One of Jacob… the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel” (vv.22-26). Benjamin is “a ravenous wolf” (v.27). Then Jacob asks to be buried in the cave of Machpelah with Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah (vv.29-32), draws his feet into the bed, breathes his last, “and he was gathered to his people” (v.33).
context.custom: A father’s last words to his sons were treated as weighty and binding, like Isaac’s blessing in chapter 27. The poem is full of wordplay on the names: Judah and “praise” (yadah), Dan and “judge” (din), Gad and “raiders” (gedud), Zebulun and “dwell.” The lion became the emblem of Judah. The meaning of “Shiloh” in v.10 is debated: it may be a title, or be read until he comes to whom it belongs, as in Ezekiel 21:27.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 50: Jacob is buried in Canaan, Joseph reassures his brothers, and Joseph dies in Egypt.
context.timelineBible: Judah, not Reuben or Joseph, receives the scepter, and David, Israel’s great king, comes from his tribe. Jewish and Christian readers alike have read v.10 of the Messiah. Revelation calls Jesus “the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David” (Revelation 5:5). Moses gives a second set of tribal blessings before his death (Deuteronomy 33).

translation.meaning: A rod, staff or scepter; also a tribe. The ruler’s rod will stay with Judah.
Shiloh, read by many as a name of the coming ruler. Others divide the letters as shelloh, “to whom it belongs.” Jewish tradition and the church both read it of the Messiah.
Salvation, deliverance. The word at the heart of the name Joshua and Jesus. Jacob breaks off his blessings to pray for it.

gospelParallels.note: The Lion of the tribe of Judah has triumphed.
The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David.

otBackground.note: Moses blesses the tribes before his death.
He chose the tribe of Judah and chose David.
Until He comes to whom it rightfully belongs.

overview.summary: On his deathbed Jacob speaks a poetic word over each of his twelve sons, giving the scepter to Judah and a rich blessing to Joseph, asks to be buried at Machpelah, and dies.

history.t: Each son’s word looks ahead to his tribe in the land.
The tribe of David and the kings of Jerusalem.

customs.t: A father’s final blessing shaped his sons’ futures.
Machpelah holds Abraham, Isaac and their wives.

archaeology.t: The traditional tomb in Hebron, under a Herodian enclosure.
The lion appears on seals of Judah’s royal officials.

overview.discussion: In the middle of blessing his sons, Jacob stopped to pray, “I await Your salvation, O LORD” (v.18). What am I waiting on God for, as I look at the people I love?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

peoplePlaces.d: A fruitful vine, prince among his brothers

biblePlaces.name: The land of Goshen, in the eastern Nile delta (approximate)

currentImage.caption: The building over the Cave of the Patriarchs (Machpelah) in Hebron. Its great stone enclosure was built by Herod the Great in the 1st century BC; tradition holds that Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah lie in the cave below (Genesis 49:29-32).
